nodes.summary: Given a tree $s$ (the left sibling), a separator key $k$ and a tree $c$ (the child) such that $s$ and $c$ are both leaves or both internal nodes, $s$ has at least one key, and, when they are internal nodes, $s$ has at least one child: the last key of $s$ is removed from $s$ and becomes the new separator, $k$ becomes the first key of $c$, and, for internal nodes, the last child of $s$ is removed from $s$ and becomes…
nodes.title: Borrowing a key from the left sibling

nodes.summary: Given a tree $c$ (the child), a separator key $k$ and a tree $s$ (the right sibling) such that $c$ and $s$ are both leaves or both internal nodes, $s$ has at least one key, and, when they are internal nodes, $s$ has at least one child: $k$ becomes the last key of $c$, the first key of $s$ is removed from $s$ and becomes the new separator, and, for internal nodes, the first child of $s$ is removed from $s$ and…
nodes.title: Borrowing a key from the right sibling

nodes.summary: A raw B-tree with keys in a type $\alpha$ is either a leaf, holding a list of keys, or an internal node, holding a list of separator keys and a list of child raw B-trees. The type imposes no invariant: that an internal node with $k$ keys has $k + 1$ children, the bounds on key counts, the balance of the tree and the ordering of the keys are imposed separately by the structural and ordering invariants of B-trees.
nodes.title: Raw B-trees

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$ and let $T$ be a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ over a linearly ordered key type. For all keys $x$ and $y$, searching for $y$ in the tree obtained by deleting $x$ from $T$ with minimum degree $t$ succeeds if and only if $y \ne x$ and $y$ is a key of $T$.
nodes.title: Search after top-down deletion

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$, let $T$ be a B-tree of minimum degree $t$, and let $x$ and $y$ be keys. The B-tree search for $y$ in the rebuilding deletion of $x$ from $T$ with minimum degree $t$ returns true if and only if $y \ne x$ and $y$ is stored in $T$.
nodes.title: Search after rebuilding deletion

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be linearly ordered and let $T$ be a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ with keys in $\alpha$. For every key $x \in \alpha$, the search procedure returns true on $x$ and $T$ if and only if $x$ is a member of $T$, that is, $x$ occurs in the inorder flattening of $T$.
nodes.title: Correctness of B-tree search

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered key type, the search for a key $x$ in a raw B-tree proceeds as follows. At a leaf, report whether $x$ is in the leaf's key list. At an internal node with separators $k_1, \dots, k_m$ and children $c_0, c_1, \dots$, scan the separators in order. On reaching $k_i$, report failure if the node has no child $c_{i-1}$; otherwise search $c_{i-1}$ if $x < k_i$, report success if $x = k_i$, and move…
nodes.title: B-tree search

nodes.summary: Given a height $h$, a minimum degree $t$, a key $x$ of a linearly ordered key type and a tree $T$, the result is defined as follows. If $T$ is a leaf, the result is the leaf whose key list is that of $T$ with the first occurrence of $x$ erased, whatever $h$ is. If $T$ is an internal node and $h = 0$, the result is $T$. If $T$ is an internal node and $h = n + 1$, the result is the internal node whose separator and…
nodes.title: Height-indexed B-tree deletion

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an operation that deletes a key from a tree, let $t$ be a natural number, let $x$ be a key of a linearly ordered key type, and write $|c|$ for the number of keys stored at the root of a tree $c$. Deleting $x$ within a node with separator list $K$ and child list $C$, using $D$ on children, produces a new separator list and a new child list. Write $k$ for the first separator, $c$ for the first child, and…
nodes.title: Deletion within a B-tree node

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$ and let $T$ be a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ over a linearly ordered key type. For every key $x$, the tree obtained by deleting $x$ from $T$ with minimum degree $t$ is again a B-tree of minimum degree $t$.
nodes.title: Top-down deletion preserves the B-tree invariant

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$. For every key $x$ and every tree $T$, whether or not $T$ is itself a B-tree, the rebuilding deletion of $x$ from $T$ with minimum degree $t$ is a B-tree of minimum degree $t$.
nodes.title: Rebuilding deletion yields a B-tree

nodes.summary: For every minimum degree $t$, key $x$ and tree $T$, the rebuilding deletion of $x$ from $T$ with minimum degree $t$ equals the tree built from the list obtained by removing the first occurrence of $x$ from the flattening of $T$, by inserting its keys from right to left into the empty tree with minimum degree $t$.
nodes.title: Rebuilding deletion unfolds to erase and rebuild

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$. For every key $x$ and every tree $T$, there is a height $h$ such that the rebuilding deletion of $x$ from $T$ with minimum degree $t$ is root-valid of minimum degree $t$ and height $h$: all leaves sit at depth $h$, every node holds at most $2t - 1$ keys, every non-root node holds at least $t - 1$ keys, an internal root holds at least one key, and an internal node with $k$ keys has $k + 1$ children.
nodes.title: Rebuilding deletion yields a root-valid tree

nodes.summary: For a minimum degree $t$, a key $x$ and a tree $T$, the rebuilding deletion of $x$ from $T$ is the tree obtained by inserting the keys of the list $L$, from right to left, into the empty tree with B-tree insertion of minimum degree $t$, where $L$ is the inorder flattening of $T$ with the first occurrence of $x$ removed ($L$ is the flattening itself when $x$ does not occur in it).
nodes.title: B-tree deletion by rebuilding

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$ and let $T$ be a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ over a linearly ordered key type. For every key $x$, the tree obtained by deleting $x$ from $T$ with minimum degree $t$ satisfies the root invariant of B-trees of minimum degree $t$ at some height.
nodes.title: Top-down deletion yields a root-valid tree

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$ and let $T$ be an ordered tree over a linearly ordered key type (its inorder flattening is strictly increasing) that satisfies the root invariant of B-trees of minimum degree $t$ at height $h$. For every key $x$, the tree obtained by deleting $x$ from $T$ with minimum degree $t$ satisfies the root invariant of minimum degree $t$ at height $h$ or at height $h - 1$, where $h - 1$ is truncated…
nodes.title: Top-down deletion lowers the height by at most one

nodes.summary: Deleting a key $x$ of a linearly ordered key type from a tree $T$ with minimum degree $t$ applies height-indexed deletion of $x$ with minimum degree $t$ to $T$ at the height of $T$, where the height of a leaf, or of an internal node without children, is $0$, and the height of any other internal node is one more than the height of its first child. If the outcome is an internal node with no keys and exactly one…
nodes.title: Top-down B-tree deletion

nodes.summary: For every key type equipped with a binary relation $<$ and every natural number $t \ge 2$, the empty B-tree is a B-tree of minimum degree $t$.
nodes.title: The empty tree is a B-tree

nodes.summary: The empty B-tree is the leaf with no keys.
nodes.title: The empty B-tree

nodes.summary: If $T$ is a B-tree of minimum degree $t$, then there is a height $h$ such that $T$ satisfies the root structural invariant of minimum degree $t$ at height $h$.
nodes.title: B-trees satisfy the root invariant

nodes.summary: For every raw B-tree $T$ and every list $s$, the accumulating flattening of $T$ with suffix $s$ equals the inorder flattening of $T$ followed by $s$.
nodes.title: The accumulating B-tree flattening is correct

nodes.summary: Given a raw B-tree $T$ and a list $s$, this returns the inorder traversal of $T$ followed by $s$. For a leaf it is the leaf's key list followed by $s$. For an internal node with separator keys $k_1, \dots, k_m$ and children $c_0, \dots, c_n$ it is the sequence $c_0, k_1, c_1, k_2, \dots$, in which children and keys alternate starting with a child until one of the two lists runs out, then the remaining keys or…
nodes.title: Accumulating flattening of a B-tree

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$ and let $T$ be a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ over a linearly ordered key type. For every key $x$, deleting $x$ from $T$ twice with minimum degree $t$ gives a tree with the same inorder flattening as deleting $x$ from $T$ once.
nodes.title: Repeated top-down deletion

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$, let $T$ be an ordered tree (its flattening is strictly increasing) and let $x$ be a key. Deleting $x$ twice by rebuilding with minimum degree $t$ gives a tree with the same flattening as deleting $x$ once.
nodes.title: Rebuilding deletion of the same key twice

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$, let $T$ be an ordered tree and let $x$ be a key that does not occur in the flattening of $T$. Then the rebuilding deletion of $x$ from $T$ with minimum degree $t$ has the same flattening as $T$.
nodes.title: Rebuilding deletion of an absent key

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$, let $T$ be an ordered tree and let $x$ be a key. The flattening of the rebuilding deletion of $x$ from $T$ with minimum degree $t$ is the flattening of $T$ with the first occurrence of $x$ removed (unchanged if $x$ does not occur).
nodes.title: Flattening after rebuilding deletion

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$ and let $T$ be a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ over a linearly ordered key type. For every key $x$, the inorder flattening of the tree obtained from $T$ by top-down deletion of $x$ with minimum degree $t$ is the flattening of $T$ with the first occurrence of $x$ removed (unchanged if $x$ does not occur).
nodes.title: Deletion from a B-tree erases the key from its flattening

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$. For every strictly increasing list $L$ of keys, the tree built from $L$ by inserting its keys from right to left into the empty tree with minimum degree $t$ has flattening exactly $L$.
nodes.title: Building a B-tree from a strictly increasing list

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be linearly ordered, let $t \ge 2$, and let $T$ be a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ with keys in $\alpha$. For every key $x \in \alpha$, the inorder flattening of the tree obtained by inserting $x$ into $T$ with minimum degree $t$ equals the sorted insertion of $x$ into the inorder flattening of $T$.
nodes.title: B-tree insertion as sorted list insertion

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$, let $T$ be an ordered tree with flattening of length $n$, and let $x$ be a key. The flattening of the rebuilding deletion of $x$ from $T$ with minimum degree $t$ has length $n - 1$ if $x$ occurs in the flattening of $T$, and length $n$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Key count after rebuilding deletion

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$, let $T$ be a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ over a linearly ordered key type, and let $x$ be a key. If $x$ occurs in the inorder flattening of $T$, the flattening of the tree obtained from $T$ by deleting $x$ (with minimum degree $t$) has length one less than the flattening of $T$; otherwise the two flattenings have the same length.
nodes.title: Deletion shortens the flattening by one exactly when the key is present

nodes.summary: Let $\alpha$ be linearly ordered, let $t \ge 2$, let $T$ be a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ with keys in $\alpha$, and let $x \in \alpha$. Let $T'$ be the tree obtained by inserting $x$ into $T$ with minimum degree $t$. If $x$ occurs in the inorder flattening of $T$, then the flattening of $T'$ has the same length as that of $T$; otherwise it is one longer.
nodes.title: Size of a B-tree after insertion

nodes.summary: Let $K_1$ and $K_2$ be lists of keys, $m$ a key, and $C_1$ and $C_2$ lists of raw B-trees such that $C_1$ has exactly one more element than $K_1$. Then the flattening of the node whose key list is $K_1$ followed by $m$ followed by $K_2$ and whose child list is $C_1$ followed by $C_2$ equals the flattening of the node with keys $K_1$ and children $C_1$, followed by $m$, followed by the flattening of the node with…
nodes.title: Splitting a node's flattening at a separator

nodes.summary: For a key $k$ and a list of keys $K$, the flattening of the node with key list $k$ followed by $K$ and no children is $k$ followed by the flattening of the node with key list $K$ and no children.
nodes.title: Flattening a childless node, one key at a time

nodes.summary: For a raw B-tree $c$ and a list $C$ of raw B-trees, the flattening of the node with no keys and child list $c$ followed by $C$ is the flattening of $c$ followed by the flattening of the node with no keys and child list $C$.
nodes.title: Flattening a keyless node, one child at a time

nodes.summary: The flattening of the internal node with no keys and no children is the empty list.
nodes.title: Flattening of the empty node

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered key type, the flattening of an ordered raw B-tree has no duplicate entries.
nodes.title: An ordered B-tree has no duplicate keys

nodes.summary: The flattening of a raw B-tree is the list of its keys defined recursively: for a leaf it is the leaf's key list, and for an internal node with keys $k_1, k_2, \dots$ and children $c_1, c_2, \dots$ it is the flattening of $c_1$, then $k_1$, then the flattening of $c_2$, then $k_2$, and so on, alternating while both lists last; whatever remains of the longer list is then appended in order, each surplus child…
nodes.title: Inorder flattening of a B-tree

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered key type, every natural number $t \ge 2$ and every list $L$ of keys, the tree obtained by inserting the elements of $L$ from right to left into the empty tree, each insertion with minimum degree $t$, is a B-tree of minimum degree $t$.
nodes.title: Building from a list yields a B-tree

nodes.summary: For a linearly ordered key type and a natural number $t$, the tree built from the empty list is the empty tree, and the tree built from a list with head $x$ and tail $L$ is the result of inserting $x$, with minimum degree $t$, into the tree built from $L$. Thus the elements are inserted from right to left.
nodes.title: B-tree built from a list

nodes.summary: The flattening of an insertion result that is a single tree is the flattening of that tree; for a result that splits into a left tree $\ell$, a promoted median key $m$ and a right tree $r$, it is the flattening of $\ell$, followed by $m$, followed by the flattening of $r$.
nodes.title: Flattening of a B-tree insertion result

nodes.summary: Over a linearly ordered key type, let $t$ be a natural number, $x$ a key, $K$ the key list of a leaf, and $K'$ the result of ordered insertion of $x$ into $K$. If $K'$ has at most $2t - 1$ keys, the insertion result is the single leaf with keys $K'$. Otherwise the leaf is split: the result consists of the leaf holding the first $t - 1$ keys of $K'$, the next key of $K'$ promoted as the median, and the leaf holding…
nodes.title: Insertion into a B-tree leaf

nodes.summary: An insertion result over a key type $\alpha$ is either a single tree over $\alpha$, or a triple $(\ell, m, r)$ of two trees $\ell$ and $r$ over $\alpha$ and a key $m$ of $\alpha$. In insertion, the first form is a subtree that did not split, and the second form is an overflowing node split into two trees of the same height, with the median key $m$ promoted between them; the type itself does not record heights.
nodes.title: Result of inserting into a B-tree subtree

nodes.summary: For minimum degree $t$ and a key $x$, insertion of $x$ into a tree returns an insertion result and is defined by recursion. At a leaf with key list $K$, it is leaf insertion of $x$ into $K$. At an internal node, the separator list and the child list are scanned together from the left. If $x$ is smaller than the current separator, or no separator is left but a child is, $x$ is inserted into the current child. If $x$…
nodes.title: Split-returning insertion into a B-tree subtree

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$ and let the keys come from a linearly ordered type. If $T$ is a B-tree of minimum degree $t$, then for every key $x$ the tree obtained by inserting $x$ into $T$ is again a B-tree of minimum degree $t$: it is ordered and root-valid at some height.
nodes.title: Insertion preserves the B-tree invariant

nodes.summary: For minimum degree $t$, the tree obtained by inserting a key $x$ into a tree $T$ is computed from the split-returning insertion of $x$ into $T$: if that returns a single tree, this tree is the result; if it returns two trees $\ell$ and $r$ with a promoted median key $m$, the result is a new root node with the single separator $m$ and the two children $\ell$ and $r$.
nodes.title: B-tree insertion

nodes.summary: A tree $T$ is a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ when $t \ge 2$ (the CLRS Chapter 18 minimum-degree requirement), $T$ is ordered, and $T$ is root-valid at some height. This is the invariant preserved by insertion and by building a tree from a list.
nodes.title: B-trees of a given minimum degree

nodes.summary: For a raw B-tree $T$, this is the length of the key list stored at the root of $T$: the number of keys of $T$ if $T$ is a leaf, and the number of separator keys of $T$ if $T$ is an internal node. Keys in the children are not counted.
nodes.title: Number of keys at the root of a B-tree

nodes.summary: For a tree $T$, the rightmost key of $T$ is an optional key defined by descending the rightmost spine: for a leaf it is the last of its keys (none if the leaf has no keys); for an internal node with at least one child it is the rightmost key of its last child; for an internal node with no children it is the last of its separator keys (none if there are none).
nodes.title: Rightmost key of a B-tree

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$ and let $T$ be a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ with keys in a linearly ordered type. For all keys $x$ and $y$, the key $y$ lies in the tree obtained from $T$ by rebuild deletion of $x$ (erasing $x$ from the inorder flattening of $T$ and rebuilding a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ from the remaining keys) if and only if $y \ne x$ and $y$ lies in $T$.
nodes.title: Membership after rebuild deletion from a B-tree

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$ and let $T$ be a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ over a linearly ordered key type. For all keys $x$ and $y$, $y$ belongs to the tree obtained from $T$ by deleting $x$ (with minimum degree $t$) if and only if $y \ne x$ and $y$ belongs to $T$.
nodes.title: Membership after deletion from a B-tree

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$ and let $xs$ be a list over a linearly ordered key type. A key $x$ belongs to the tree of minimum degree $t$ built from $xs$ (by inserting the elements of $xs$ into the empty tree, from right to left) if and only if $x$ is an element of $xs$.
nodes.title: Membership in a B-tree built from a list

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$ and let $T$ be a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ over a linearly ordered key type. For all keys $x$ and $y$, $y$ belongs to the tree obtained by inserting $x$ into $T$ if and only if $y = x$ or $y$ belongs to $T$.
nodes.title: Membership after B-tree insertion

nodes.summary: A key $x$ belongs to a tree $T$ when $x$ occurs in the inorder flattening of $T$.
nodes.title: Membership in a B-tree

nodes.summary: Given a key $s$ and trees $L$ and $R$, the merge of $L$ and $R$ around $s$ is defined as follows. If $L$ and $R$ are leaves with key lists $k_1$ and $k_2$, it is the leaf with keys $k_1$, then $s$, then $k_2$. If $L$ and $R$ are internal nodes with key lists $k_1, k_2$ and child lists $c_1, c_2$, it is the internal node with keys $k_1$, then $s$, then $k_2$, and children $c_1$ followed by $c_2$. In every other case…
nodes.title: Merging two B-tree nodes around a separator

nodes.summary: For a tree $T$, the leftmost key of $T$ is an optional key defined by descending the leftmost spine: for a leaf it is the first of its keys (none if the leaf has no keys); for an internal node with at least one child it is the leftmost key of its first child; for an internal node with no children it is the first of its separator keys (none if there are none).
nodes.title: Leftmost key of a B-tree

nodes.summary: For minimum degree $t$, a separator list $K$ and a child list $C$, the result is the internal node with separators $K$ and children $C$, kept as a single tree when $K$ has at most $2t - 1$ keys, and otherwise split by node splitting into two nodes and a promoted median key.
nodes.title: Rebuilding an internal node after insertion

nodes.summary: If an internal node with separator list $K$ is ordered, then $K$ is strictly increasing: every key of $K$ is smaller than every key that comes after it in $K$.
nodes.title: The separator keys of an ordered node are sorted

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$ and let $T$ be a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ with keys in a linearly ordered type. For every key $x$, the tree obtained from $T$ by rebuild deletion of $x$ (erasing $x$ from the inorder flattening of $T$ and rebuilding a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ from the remaining keys) does not contain $x$.
nodes.title: The deleted key is absent after rebuild deletion

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$ and let $T$ be a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ over a linearly ordered key type. For every key $x$, $x$ does not belong to the tree obtained from $T$ by deleting $x$ (with minimum degree $t$).
nodes.title: The deleted key is absent after deletion from a B-tree

nodes.summary: If a tree is a B-tree of minimum degree $t$, then it is ordered: each key of its inorder flattening is less than every key that comes after it.
nodes.title: B-trees are ordered

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$ and let keys come from a linearly ordered type. For every key $x$ and every tree $T$, not necessarily ordered, the tree obtained from $T$ by rebuild deletion of $x$ (removing the first occurrence of $x$, if any, from the inorder flattening of $T$ and rebuilding a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ from the remaining keys) is ordered: its inorder flattening is strictly increasing.
nodes.title: Rebuild deletion yields an ordered tree

nodes.summary: Let $t \ge 2$ and let $T$ be a B-tree of minimum degree $t$ over a linearly ordered key type. For every key $x$, the tree obtained from $T$ by deleting $x$ (with minimum degree $t$) is ordered: its inorder flattening is strictly increasing.
nodes.title: Deletion from a B-tree yields an ordered tree

nodes.summary: A B-tree over a type with a relation $<$ is ordered when its inorder flattening is strictly increasing, that is, each key of the flattening is less than every key that comes after it. This single condition packages sortedness of the keys at each node and the separator bounds between a node's keys and the keys stored in its subtrees.
nodes.title: Ordered B-tree

nodes.summary: Let $K_1$ and $K_2$ be lists of keys, $k$ a key, and $C_1$ and $C_2$ lists of B-trees such that $C_1$ has exactly one more tree than $K_1$ has keys. If the internal node whose key list is $K_1$ followed by $k$ followed by $K_2$, and whose child list is $C_1$ followed by $C_2$, is ordered, then every key in the flattening of the node with keys $K_1$ and children $C_1$ is less than $k$, and $k$ is less than every key…
nodes.title: Separator bounds in an ordered B-tree node

nodes.summary: For a nonempty list $l$, the result is the pair consisting of $l$ with its last element removed and the last element of $l$; for the empty list there is no result.
nodes.title: Splitting off the last element of a list

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a minimum degree, $s = t - 1$ (so $s = 0$ when $t = 0$), $k_1, \dots, k_m$ a list of keys and $c_1, \dots, c_n$ a list of B-trees. If $m > s$, splitting returns the pair of internal nodes formed by the keys $k_1, \dots, k_s$ with the first $t$ children (all of them if $n < t$) and by the keys $k_{s+2}, \dots, k_m$ with the children after the first $t$, together with the key $k_{s+1}$ promoted between…
nodes.title: Splitting a B-tree node

nodes.summary: The height of a B-tree is computed by following first children: a leaf has height $0$, an internal node with no children has height $0$, and an internal node whose first child is $c$ has height one more than the height of $c$.
nodes.title: Height of a B-tree along first children

nodes.summary: If a tree is a B-tree of minimum degree $t$, then $t \ge 2$.
nodes.title: The minimum degree of a B-tree is at least two

nodes.summary: If a tree satisfies the root invariant for minimum degree $t$ at height $h$, then for some natural number $m$ it satisfies the structural invariant for minimum degree $t$, minimum top-node key count $m$ and height $h$.
nodes.title: Root-valid B-trees are valid

nodes.summary: For a minimum degree $t$ and a height $h$, a tree satisfies the root invariant when either $h = 0$ and the tree is a leaf with at most $2t - 1$ keys (possibly none, for the empty tree), or $h = h' + 1$ and the tree is an internal node with between $1$ and $2t - 1$ keys and exactly one more child than keys, every child satisfying the structural invariant for minimum degree $t$, minimum top-node key count $t - 1$ and…
nodes.title: Root invariant of a B-tree

nodes.summary: For a minimum degree $t$ and a minimum key count $m$ for the top node, the invariant is defined inductively over the height: a leaf with $k$ keys satisfies it at height $0$ when $m \le k \le 2t - 1$, and for every natural number $h$, an internal node with $k$ keys satisfies it at height $h + 1$ when $m \le k \le 2t - 1$, the node has exactly $k + 1$ children, and every child satisfies the invariant with minimum key…

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
